title: Private deployments: VPC & On-prem deployment guide, day-2 ops, upgrade and rollback, and customer requirements library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended guidance for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem), including reference architectures, on-prem packaging formats, day-2 operational procedures, upgrade and rollback playbooks, and a customer requirements checklist. It is intended for engineers delivering Private deployments and for solutions engineers aligning customer expectations before kickoff.

Goals
- Provide repeatable, auditable deployment and day-2 operations guidance.
- Minimize downtime during upgrades and model rollouts.
- Define required customer network/security/storage requirements early in the sales cycle.
- Provide runbook actions for common day-2 events.

Table of contents
1) Scope and assumptions
2) High-level reference architectures
3) On-prem packaging and installation artifacts
4) Deployment checklist and automated tasks
5) Day-2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling, troubleshooting)
6) Upgrade and rollback procedures (control plane, runtime, models)
7) Customer requirements library (network, security, capacity)
8) Ownership, SLAs, and escalation path
9) Appendix: CLI examples, sample manifests, and templates

1) Scope and assumptions
- This document covers Private: VPC-hosted (customer VPC with Redwood private control plane) and fully on-prem deployments (air-gapped or restricted environments).
- Assumes customer provides compute (K8s clusters or host fleet), networking, and optional HSM/KMS. Redwood provides the Private control plane (optionally run as managed control plane), container images, Helm charts, and operator components.
- Supported GPU types: NVIDIA A100, H100, and equivalent accelerator classes. CPU-only deployments are supported for small embedding workloads but not recommended for production generation.

2) High-level reference architectures
A. VPC-hosted private (recommended for most enterprise customers)
- Components: customer VPC (subnets for workload and infra), private-control-plane endpoints (TLS + mTLS), model-serving K8s cluster (GPU nodes), NAT/GW for egress, Transit Gateway or Direct Connect for predictable network, KMS integration, monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana) and logging (ELK or hosted SIEM), and optional HSM for key storage.
- Network flow summary: client -> customer app -> internal service mesh -> Redwood inference gateway (in-cluster) -> model serving pods -> GPU nodes.
- Availability zones: recommend 3 AZs for critical workloads; deploy serving pools across zones with cross-AZ fallback routing.

B. On-prem / air-gapped reference (for regulated customers)
- Components: private control plane deployed in customer DMZ or air-gapped control cluster (synchronized via approved CICD channels), isolated model-serving cluster with dedicated GPU racks, on-prem object store (S3 compatible) or NVMe-backed filesystem for model artifacts, on-prem Prometheus + loki for metrics/logs, and KMS/HSM integration via customer hardware.
- Packaging: offline tarball including images, Helm charts, operator binaries, and signed artifact manifest.

Reference architecture diagram (textual)
- Control plane (managed or self-hosted) -> API gateway (internal) -> Inference router (per-tenant) -> Serving pool(s) (GPU node pool, autoscaler) -> KV cache / prefix cache (in-memory + redis optional) -> Model artifact store (S3/NFS)

3) On-prem packaging and installation artifacts
- Primary distribution formats:
  - Online Helm charts (recommended for VPC): chart repo (signed) + values templates.
  - Offline bundle (recommended for air-gapped): tar.gz containing container images as tar archives, Helm charts, operator binaries, license file, and a signed manifest.json.
- Versioning and signing:
  - All releases use semver: e.g. rpd-2026.2.1. Artifact manifests contain SHA256 checksums and GPG signatures.
  - Controls: operator verifies manifest signature before applying.
- Preflight installer (rpi-install.sh) performs environment checks: kernel version, NVIDIA drivers, nv_peer_mem, kubernetes version (>=1.24 and <=1.28 tested), CRI-O or containerd running, required ports open.

4) Deployment checklist and automated tasks
Pre-deployment (customer + Redwood alignment)
1. Confirm capacity and GPU types (see Customer Requirements section).
2. Exchange network allowlist entries and IP ranges for control plane endpoints.
3. Confirm KMS/HSM integration approach and key policy.
4. Validate required object storage endpoints and credentials.
5. Schedule maintenance window for initial install (2-4 hours typical).

Automated tasks executed by installer
- Create namespaces and RBAC roles.
- Install CRDs and operators.
- Seed model artifact bucket with signed model tarballs.
- Bootstrap metrics exporters and Prometheus scraping jobs.

Minimal manual steps (examples)
- Apply Helm values for cloud-specific settings: imagePullSecrets, proxy settings, storage classes.
- Configure secrets via sealed-secrets or HSM-backed secret store.

5) Day-2 operations
Monitoring and alerting (recommended thresholds)
- Metrics to monitor:
  - per-model p50/p95 latency (goal p95 < 300ms for single-turn gen on A100 for 4k context),
  - tokens/sec per GPU,
  - GPU memory utilization (alert > 85%),
  - KV cache hit rate (alert < 60% for cache-heavy workloads),
  - container restarts and OOM events,
  - disk I/O saturation on model artifact mounts.
- Suggested alerts:
  - GPU count below configured pool size (P0: page oncall),
  - sustained p95 latency degradation > 2x baseline for 15 minutes (P1),
  - model artifact store errors (P1),
  - control plane heartbeats missing for > 2 minutes (P0).

Backups and artifacts
- Model artifacts: keep immutable copies in S3-compatible storage. Retain last 3 production model versions by default.
- Operator and control plane DB snapshots: daily snapshots retained 30 days; immediate snapshot before upgrades.

Scaling and capacity management
- Horizontal scaling: use autoscaler that respects GPU packing policies. Recommend target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds: scale-up when GPU utilization > 70% for 5m, scale-down when < 30% for 15m.
- Warm pools: maintain a small warm pool (10% of peak) to reduce cold-start latency for new models.

Routine maintenance and patching
- Kernel and driver patching window: quarterly; follow N-2 driver compatibility testing.
- Container runtime security patching: apply node-by-node rolling updates with cordon/drain and verify model-serving readiness on each node post-update.

Common troubleshooting playbooks (short)
- Pod OOM or GPU OOM:
  1. Check pod logs and NVIDIA DCGM metrics.
  2. Check model shard size and batch config; reduce max_batch_size or max_seq_length if necessary.
  3. If persistent, scale up GPU pool or change instance SKU.
- Increased latency for specific model:
  1. Confirm KV cache hit rate and recent cache evictions.
  2. Check concurrent request queue length and batching window.
  3. If traffic spike, consider serving a quantized variant temporarily.

6) Upgrade and rollback procedures
Principles
- Zero-impact model inference is the goal; upgrades should be staged and deterministic.
- Always take snapshots of control plane state and model artifact metadata prior to upgrade.
- Use canary rollouts for control plane and runtime changes.

A. Control plane upgrade (managed or self-hosted)
Pre-upgrade checks:
- Validate backups exist and are restorable.
- Confirm no ongoing model uploads or active rollouts.
- Ensure last_updated state present in related status page.

Upgrade steps (rolling canary)
1. Prepare release on candidate cluster (1 node) and run smoke tests: health checks, API auth, basic inference test.
2. Promote to 10% of control plane replicas and run end-to-end stress tests (10 minutes).
3. If smoke tests pass, proceed with rolling upgrade across remaining replicas with sequential restarts and post-checks.
4. Monitor metrics for 30m; if anomalies, trigger rollback.

Rollback
- If rollback required, use stored control plane snapshot and reapply previous Helm revision.
- Steps: scale down new control plane replicas, re-apply previous chart version, restore DB snapshot if needed, verify operator reconnection.

B. Serving runtime upgrade (inference engine, kernels)
Pre-upgrade
- Snapshot runtime config and current operator config.
- Take model serving snapshot and record active model versions.
Upgrade (canary + phased)
1. Select a low-traffic model pool as canary (e.g., test namespace).
2. Upgrade serving runtime on a subset of nodes (10-20%) and run end-to-end inference tests including latency, throughput, and output quality checks using saved prompt set.
3. Gradually increase rollout if metrics and quality pass.
Rollback
1. Drain impacted nodes.
2. Revert container image to previous tagged release via Helm rollback.
3. Rejoin nodes and validate model output.

C. Model version rollout and rollback (production-safe)
- Use algorithmic canary: route 1% of traffic to new model for 30 minutes, check quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine similarity thresholds and product metrics), increase to 10%, 50%, 100%.
- Automated rollback triggers: quality regression above tolerance, error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, or unacceptable latency degradation.

7) Customer requirements library (quick checklist)
Network
- Public control plane endpoints: customer must allow outbound TLS to these IP ranges (provided at contract).
- Ports: 443 (control plane), 5671/5672 if using internal messaging, 9100 (node exporters), 9090 (Prometheus), 9411 (tracing) - adjust to customer policy.
- Private connectivity options: Direct Connect / ExpressRoute / IPsec VPN.

Compute and storage
- Kubernetes support: K8s 1.24-1.28 supported; at least 3 master nodes and 3 worker nodes for HA for production.
- GPU SKUs: A100/H100 recommended; NVMe-backed local storage for model sharding.
- Storage: S3-compatible object store with 1GB/s throughput for model artifacts for large fleets.

Security and compliance
- Identity: OIDC or SAML for control plane admin; RBAC mapped to org roles.
- Key management: customer KMS/HSM recommended for production keys; rotation policy required.
- Audit logging: must be shipped to customer SIEM or stored for 12+ months per enterprise policy.

Observability
- Prometheus scrape targets must be reachable from monitoring plane.
- Log retention and forwarding to central ELK/loki must be configured.

Operational SLAs and expectations
- Initial install: Redwood provides 4hr install support window (3 engineers) for first deployment.
- Ongoing response: P0 page within 15 minutes, P1 acknowledge within 1 hour under enterprise support.

8) Ownership, SLAs, and escalation path
- Ownership matrix:
  - Redwood Platform (owner): control plane, operators, container images, official runbooks.
  - Customer (owner): underlying hardware, network, HSM, storage.
  - Joint (owner): backup and restore testing, security patching cadence.
- Escalation path (short):
  1. Customer oncall -> Redwood Solutions Engineer -> Redwood Platform SRE -> Escalate to eng oncall -> Exec oncall if > 8 hours

9) Appendix: CLI examples, sample manifests, and templates
A. Preflight command (example)
# run on cluster control plane node
./rpi-install.sh --preflight --kubeconfig=/root/.kube/config --driver-check

B. Sample Helm values (snip)
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: registry.redwood-inference/private
  tag: rpd-2026.2.1
resources:
  requests:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
autoscaling:
  enabled: true
  targetGPUUtilization: 70

C. Upgrade checklist template
- [ ] Snapshot control plane DB (timestamp: __ )
- [ ] Snapshot model artifact manifest
- [ ] Run canary on test namespace
- [ ] Run smoke tests (auth, basic inference)
- [ ] Increase rollout to 10% and verify metrics
- [ ] Complete rolling upgrade
